## Description

Everyone is talking about AI, but few accountants have had a calm, practical introduction. This session demystifies large language models (LLMs) in plain accounting language: what they are, why they sometimes sound confident and wrong, and how the major tools (Claude, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT) compare. We then get hands-on with prompts that save real time on routine work, with clear guardrails around confidentiality and professional skepticism. You leave with a short list of use cases you can apply at your desk the very next day.

## Length

4 hours.

## Key Takeaways

Upon completion of this course, you will understand:

- What an LLM is and is not, in non-technical terms (tokens, training data, hallucinations, why answers vary)
- How the major LLM tools differ, and how to choose among them for a given task
- The anatomy of a good prompt: role, task, context, format and constraints
- What data is safe to share with an AI tool, and how to work within your organization's policy
- How to check AI output with professional skepticism before it reaches a reviewer, client or auditor
- A personal list of three to five high-value use cases for your own role

## Workflows We Will Work Through

Hands-on exercises use realistic, simulated (never confidential) data. Examples across functions and industries include:

- Controllership: draft a plain-English explanation of a technical accounting standard for a non-finance stakeholder
- FP&A: turn a variance table into first-draft management commentary
- Audit and assurance: summarize a long process narrative and draft follow-up questions
- Tax: outline a research question and the factors to consider before consulting authoritative sources
- Any role: summarize a long email thread or policy document, and draft a clear reply

Exercises are tool-agnostic. You can follow along with Claude, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot or ChatGPT, whichever your organization permits.

## Target Audience

- **Staff and senior accountants** curious about AI who want a safe, practical starting point
- **Managers and controllers** who need to understand what their teams are doing with AI, and where the risks are
- **Accountants across industries** (public accounting, corporate finance, nonprofit, government, banking, healthcare and more)

## Prerequisite(s)

No technical background or programming experience is required. Please bring a laptop and an account with at least one LLM tool (a free tier is fine). We will cover choosing one in the "Before We Start" guide.
